Hi, Tom! Did you choose the place for the team offsite?
Not yet. I have three options: Zurich, Lucerne or Basel. Can you help me?
Sure. Which one is the most convenient?
Zurich. The hotel is next to the airport, but it's the most expensive: four hundred francs a night.
Wow. And Lucerne?
Lucerne is the most beautiful. The hotel is small and cozy, with an impressive view of the lake. But it's the farthest from the airport.
And the conference center in Basel?
It's the most affordable, and it has the biggest meeting room. Basel isn't the liveliest city, but the trains are very reliable.
We are forty people, so Basel is the best choice. And we can have the team dinner in Lucerne!
Great idea. A dinner by the lake is worth it.

Hi everyone, and welcome back to my channel. Today: the three best neighborhoods in São Paulo for a business trip. Number one is Faria Lima. It is not the cheapest area, but it is the most convenient, because many big companies have offices there. Number two is Vila Madalena. It is the liveliest neighborhood in the city, with small, cozy bars and a lot of street art. It is the best place for dinner after a long day at work. Number three is Liberdade. It is one of the most affordable areas, and the Japanese food there is the most impressive in the city. My advice: avoid the subway at six p.m. That is the most crowded time of the day. And remember, Paulista Avenue on a Sunday is worth it. They close it to cars, and it is full of music and people.

Welcome back to Travel Stories. I'm Daniel. Today I want to answer a question from a listener: what is the best way to travel around Switzerland? I tried three ways. First, the car. It was the most flexible option, but parking in Zurich was the most expensive part of my trip. Second, the plane. It was the fastest way from Zurich to Geneva, but the airport was crowded, and for a very short trip, the flight was not worth it. Third, the train. For me, the train was the best way. Swiss trains are the most reliable trains I know. They are clean, spacious and always on time. And the views from the window are the most impressive in Europe. So my answer is simple: take the train.

The inn in Lucerne is the coziest, with the most impressive view of the lake. The conference center in Basel is the most affordable, and it has the biggest meeting room. In the end, Aline and Tom choose Basel, because it is the best option for forty people.
